forces.title: Heightened regulatory compliance in BFSI drives IT services demand
forces.description: RBI's new Master Directions, effective July 2026, consolidate and heighten regulatory expectations for technology, cybersecurity, operational resilience, and assurance across financial entities. This creates a significant tailwind for IT Services & Outsourcing firms, as financial institutions require specialized consulting, cybersecurity services, and system integration support to meet stringent compliance mandates, particularly concerning third-party technology arrangements and expedited cyber incident reporting obligations.
forces.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

forces.title: Agentic AI shifts from experimentation to enterprise adoption
forces.description: Agentic AI is moving from an experimental phase to widespread enterprise adoption, with 88% of enterprises investing in its integration. This structural change means the bottleneck is no longer technology availability but effective integration into complex business processes, legacy environments, and governance structures. This evolution creates high demand for IT services firms offering specialized AI integration, deployment, and governance capabilities to help clients operationalize AI safely and at scale.
forces.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

forces.title: AI becoming strategic necessity in cybersecurity operations
forces.description: AI is transforming cybersecurity from an emerging technology to a strategic necessity for organizations. As threat actors increasingly leverage AI for sophisticated and large-scale attacks, IT services firms are experiencing growing demand for AI-enabled cybersecurity solutions. This structural shift drives opportunities for providing comprehensive services across the cybersecurity lifecycle—including advanced threat detection, automated response, and AI governance—to strengthen enterprise resilience.

forces.title: Critical cybersecurity talent shortage exacerbated by AI
forces.description: A critical global shortage of cybersecurity talent is worsening due to the rapid advancement of AI, which is widening the advanced skills gap. This poses a significant risk to IT Services & Outsourcing firms, as it challenges their ability to deliver advanced security solutions and meet client demand. Firms must invest heavily in upskilling their workforce in strategic areas like AI security, cloud security, and cyber resilience to remain competitive.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity in the Age of AI

forces.title: GCCs increasingly owning core processes and niche capabilities
forces.description: Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in India are evolving beyond cost efficiency to drive strategic value, increasingly owning core business processes in verticals like retail and CPG, and focusing on niche skills and transformation. This trend presents a significant headwind for third-party IT Services & Outsourcing firms (IN080101), as companies are building these high-value capabilities captively, intensifying competition for talent and potentially reducing external outsourcing opportunities.
forces.source_title: How India GCCs are driving core retail and CPG value

forces.title: Robust growth in India's public cloud services market
forces.description: India's public cloud services market is experiencing robust growth, projected to reach US$ 30.4 billion by 2029 with a 22.6% CAGR from US$ 10.9 billion in 2024. This accelerated demand, driven by sectors like BFSI, manufacturing, government, software, and media, creates a significant tailwind for IT Services & Outsourcing firms. Opportunities abound in cloud migration, managed services, and developing cloud-native applications.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Government digitalization and AI mission initiatives driving demand
forces.description: Significant government funding and policy support, including the IndiaAI Mission's US$ 1.25 billion outlay and allocations for cybersecurity, are driving overall IT demand. These initiatives accelerate digitalization across sectors, foster AI adoption, and enhance digital public infrastructure. This robust government backing creates a substantial tailwind for IT Services & Outsourcing firms, generating new project opportunities and expanding the addressable market for advanced technology services.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Data quality and ethical concerns hinder AI implementation
forces.description: The effective implementation of AI in enterprises is hindered by significant challenges related to data quality, governance, and ethical concerns. Nearly 53% of Indian CEOs believe their data is not sufficiently AI-ready, and 62% cite ethical concerns as a barrier. For IT Services & Outsourcing firms, this represents a key risk as it complicates AI project delivery and necessitates specialized services to establish robust data foundations, governance frameworks, and address biases for trusted AI deployment.
forces.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

forces.title: Shift from 'per-FTE' to outcome-based pricing models
forces.description: The IT services industry is undergoing a structural shift from traditional 'per-FTE' (Full-Time Equivalent) contracts to outcome-based pricing models. This change is driven by clients demanding 'pay-for-results' due to expected productivity gains from AI (20-40%). This forces IT Services & Outsourcing firms to adapt their business models, offering more fixed-price, subscription, and usage-based deals, which requires a deeper focus on demonstrable value and efficiency.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Strong demand from BFSI vertical for IT services
forces.description: The BFSI sector remains a key business vertical for the IT Services & Outsourcing industry, projected to see 7-9% revenue growth for IT services in FY26. This strong demand is driven by increased IT spending for competitive advantage, extensive digitalization, and generative AI initiatives, despite the escalating cybersecurity risks. This sustained investment provides a significant tailwind for firms specializing in financial services technology solutions.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: India's large developer workforce provides talent advantage
forces.description: India boasts the world's largest developer workforce with over 5.4 million software engineers and produces 500,000 new graduates annually. This abundant talent pool, coupled with India leading globally in AI talent acquisition (33% annual hiring rate), provides a significant competitive advantage for IT Services & Outsourcing firms. This ensures a consistent supply of skilled professionals to meet growing domestic and international demand, bolstering service delivery capabilities.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Increased M&A activity for niche IT skills
forces.description: The IT sector is witnessing a surge in M&A activity, with approximately 135 tech deals worth US$ 1.7 billion in H1 2025. This increased deal-making is driven by firms' strategic need to acquire niche skills and expand capabilities in high-growth areas such as cloud, AI, and cybersecurity. This cyclical change indicates a period of industry consolidation and strategic repositioning, affecting competition and service offerings for IT Services & Outsourcing firms.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Rapidly increasing cyber incidents impacting BFSI sector
forces.description: Cyber incidents in India have doubled over the last four years, with the BFSI sector experiencing significant breaches due to cloud misconfigurations, ransomware, and sophisticated heists. Mid-tier BFSI firms are particularly vulnerable given their aggressive digitalization, interconnectedness through shared infrastructure, and comparatively limited cybersecurity budgets. This escalating threat landscape poses a key risk to financial clients and drives urgent demand for advanced cybersecurity services from IN080101 providers.
forces.source_title: Cybersecurity in the Age of AI

forces.title: Geopolitical instability and economic uncertainty persist
forces.description: The global economic landscape remains uncertain, heavily influenced by evolving geopolitical dynamics, such as the US-Iran conflict, and volatile energy prices. This persistent instability translates into a headwind for IT Services & Outsourcing firms through cautious client spending, potential currency depreciation risks, and increased operational costs. India's reliance on imported energy exacerbates its economic vulnerability, requiring adaptive policy and business strategies for resilience.

forces.title: Non-metro cities emerge as new IT growth and talent hubs
forces.description: Non-metro cities in India are emerging as significant growth and employment hubs for the IT sector, driving over 50% of IT hiring growth in H1 2025. These tier-2 and tier-3 cities offer substantial cost savings (around 30%) and are attracting demand in AI, cloud, and cybersecurity. This trend presents an upside driver for IT Services & Outsourcing firms to expand operations, tap into new talent pools, and achieve greater operational efficiency outside traditional metro centers.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

viewpoints.title: RBI's new tech directives boost IT services demand from BFSI
viewpoints.description: KPMG notes that RBI's consolidated Master Directions on technology, cybersecurity, and operational resilience for financial entities create significant demand for IT services. These directives require institutions to align controls and governance, particularly impacting third-party technology arrangements and cyber incident reporting. This regulatory push necessitates specialized IT consulting, cybersecurity services, and system integration support for compliance within the BFSI sector.
viewpoints.source_title: RBI’s technology focused master directions issued on 31 July 2026

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI adoption creates significant opportunities for IT services
viewpoints.description: KPMG indicates that the transition of Agentic AI from experimentation to enterprise-wide adoption presents substantial opportunities for IT services firms. The challenge lies in integrating autonomous agents into complex business processes, legacy environments, and establishing new governance models. This fundamental shift necessitates specialized deployment capabilities and cross-functional operating models, directly benefiting IT consulting and system integration services.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

viewpoints.title: AI transforming cybersecurity into strategic necessity for IT services
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that AI is reshaping cybersecurity into a strategic necessity, moving beyond mere experimentation. As threat actors leverage AI for sophisticated attacks, organizations are increasingly turning to AI to strengthen their defenses and build resilience. This creates a strong positive outlook for IT services firms providing comprehensive AI-enabled cybersecurity solutions across the entire security lifecycle, from governance to response and recovery.

viewpoints.title: India's IT services market poised for robust growth by 2034
viewpoints.description: IBEF projects a robust growth trajectory for India's IT services market, forecasting it to reach US$ 78.1 billion by 2034 from US$ 42.7 billion in 2025, driven by a 6.94% CAGR. This expansion is attributed to accelerated digital transformation initiatives, strong export demand from new verticals, and significant government support for AI and digital infrastructure projects, underscoring a positive outlook for the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Indian BFSI shows limited AI cyber readiness, creating IT services opportunity
viewpoints.description: BCG India reveals that Indian BFSI institutions exhibit limited confidence and significant gaps in their readiness for AI-enabled cyber incidents and security controls compared to global peers. Only a minority have deployed core AI security controls at scale, leaving substantial room for improvement in AI governance, agent monitoring, and guardrails. This presents a critical opportunity for IT services firms to offer specialized consulting, risk assessment, and deployment services to address these shortcomings.
viewpoints.source_title: Cybersecurity in the Age of AI
